svg.title: OSI layer stack: what you see at each layer in a packet capture
svg.desc: Seven bands, layer 7 at the top. Layer 7 application: an HTTP GET for /api/v1/users over HTTP/2 and a DNS query for the A record of api.example.com, seen with curl -v, dig and browser DevTools. Layer 6 presentation: TLS ClientHello, ServerHello, certificate and encrypted payload, UTF-8 and gzip, seen with openssl s_client and the Wireshark TLS dissector. Layer 5 session: TLS session ID or ticket for resumption, rarely visible as a separate layer. Layer 4 transport: TCP source port 52431, destination port 443, sequence 1001, acknowledgment 5001, ACK flag, window 65535 and options MSS 1460, SACK and timestamps, seen with ss, netstat and tcpdump. Layer 3 network: IPv4 from 10.0.1.50 to 203.0.113.10, TTL 64, protocol TCP (6), seen with ping, traceroute, ip route and tcpdump. Layer 2 data link: Ethernet source MAC aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, destination MAC 11:22:33:44:55:66, type 0x0800 and the FCS, seen with ip link, ip neigh, tcpdump -e and arp -n. Layer 1 physical: 1000BASE-T electrical signals on Cat6 copper at 1 Gbps, not visible in captures, checked with ethtool, a cable tester or the link LED.
svg.text: OSI layer stack — what you see at each layer in a packet capture
DNS: Query A record for api.example.com
TLS: ClientHello, ServerHello, Certificate, Encrypted payload
Tool: openssl s_client, Wireshark TLS dissector
TLS Session ID / Ticket for resumption
(Rarely visible as a separate layer in captures)
TCP: SrcPort=52431, DstPort=443, Seq=1001, Ack=5001, Flags=[ACK]
Tool: ping, traceroute, ip route, tcpdump 'host 10.0.1.50'
Tool: ip link, ip neigh, tcpdump -e, arp -n
1000BASE-T: electrical signals on Cat6 copper at 1 Gbps
Not visible in packet captures — below the capture point
Tool: ethtool, cable tester, looking at the link LED
